title: Office transfers slow while the neighboring test radio operates
scenario: Users near the office AP report slow file transfers at some times of day. The office AP and a test AP in the next room both use 2.4 GHz with 20 MHz channels. You record the channels, then switch the test AP's radio off and on several times while nothing else changes.

exhibits.title: Radio inventory
exhibits.text:
OFFICE-AP: channel 1, SSID OFFICE
TEST-AP: channel 3, SSID TEST
Client near OFFICE-AP: strong desired signal throughout the test

exhibits.title: Repeated controlled observation
exhibits.text:
TEST-AP transmitting: OFFICE client retries rise sharply; transfer rate falls
TEST-AP radio disabled: retries return near baseline; transfer rate recovers
Repeat trials reproduce the same result; the OFFICE channel remains 1

question: What cause is supported by the combined evidence?
options: A weak desired signal caused by increasing client distance
Interference from overlapping occupied channels 1 and 3
Co-channel contention because the SSIDs have different names
A DFS radar response on the office's 2.4 GHz channel
explanation: Channels 1 and 3 overlap, so each AP hears the other as noise it cannot decode. That is adjacent-channel interference: frames are damaged and retried, which matches the rising retries. The on/off test confirms the test AP as the source. A strong signal does not rule interference out.
fix: Move the test AP to a channel that does not overlap channel 1: channel 6 or 11 in the 1/6/11 plan. Change one radio only, then repeat the same transfer and compare the retry rate with the baseline.

title: One client cannot rejoin after the WLAN security change
scenario: The STAFF WLAN is changed from WPA2-Personal to WPA3-Personal only. The passphrase stays the same. Most clients reconnect, but one older laptop can no longer join. You compare the WLAN settings with what the laptop's driver reports it supports.

exhibits.title: WLAN settings
exhibits.text:
SSID: STAFF
Band: 5 GHz
Security: WPA3-Personal only
Authentication: SAE
PMF: Required

exhibits.title: Client capability evidence
exhibits.text:
Radio support: 802.11a/n/ac
WPA2-Personal + CCMP: Supported
PMF: Supported
WPA3-Personal / SAE: Not supported by installed OS/driver

question: Which mismatch prevents this client's access?
options: The shared passphrase differs even though it was verified unchanged
The presence of an 802.11ax AP necessarily excludes 802.11ac clients
The client lacks the SAE authentication capability required by this WLAN
The client lacks CCMP even though the capability report lists support
explanation: WPA3-Personal authenticates with SAE, and this laptop's driver does not support SAE. Supporting CCMP and PMF is not enough, and the radio standard (802.11ac) has nothing to do with the security method.
fix: Update the laptop's OS or wireless driver if a version with WPA3 support exists; otherwise replace the adapter. If the laptop must stay, the WLAN has to accept WPA2-Personal again on 2.4 or 5 GHz, where that client still gets only WPA2 protection. WPA2 cannot be enabled on a 6 GHz WLAN.
